parts.title: A repair café in town
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When a toaster stopped working, I nearly put it in the bin. Then my neighbour told me about the repair café at the community centre. It opens one Saturday a month, and volunteers help visitors repair small household objects. I was unsure whether I could fix anything, but the volunteer showed me how to test the cable safely. The toaster worked again after ten minutes.

The café is not a shop, and the volunteers do not promise that every object can be repaired. People bring old lamps, toys and clothes, and they learn by watching or helping. Last month, a retired electrician taught two teenagers how to replace a plug. They came back this week with a radio they had repaired at home.

My favourite part is the friendly atmosphere. Visitors can have tea while they wait, and someone usually brings a cake. The project also has a practical benefit: fewer things are thrown away. The organisers hope to open on two Saturdays each month, but they need more volunteers before they can do that.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer visit the repair café?
options: The writer wanted to repair a toaster.
The community centre was selling kitchen equipment.
questions.explanation: Her toaster stopped working and a neighbour told her about the café, so she went there to repair the toaster.

questions.prompt: What did the volunteer do first?
options: Explained how to test the cable safely.
Replaced the toaster with another one.
Asked the writer to buy a new tool.
questions.explanation: The volunteer showed her how to test the cable safely, and then the toaster worked again.

questions.prompt: What happened to the two teenagers?
options: They opened a repair café at home.
They returned after repairing a radio themselves.
questions.explanation: The teenagers came back this week with a radio they had repaired at home.

questions.prompt: What does the writer like about the café?
questions.explanation: Her favourite part is the friendly atmosphere, which means it is welcoming.

questions.prompt: What do the organisers need before opening more often?
questions.explanation: They need more volunteers, which means additional helpers, before they can open two Saturdays a month.

parts.title: A new cycle route
parts.instructions: Five sentences have been removed from the text. Choose the correct sentence for each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage: Last year, the town council asked residents how to make short journeys easier. [1] Many people said they would cycle if they felt safer near the busy shopping street. [2] The council painted a cycle lane and added signs at both ends. Work began in March, just before the weather became warmer. [3] During the first week, volunteers stood nearby and explained how to use the new route. They also asked cyclists to report any problems. [4] One corner was difficult to see, so the council moved a small sign. Since then, more parents have used the route to take their children to school. [5] The council now plans to connect it to the railway station.
sentences: The most common suggestion was a protected route into the centre.
In response, they planned a route away from the main road.
Local cyclists were invited to test the lane when it opened.
This quick change made the crossing clearer.
The council is also offering free bicycle lessons next month.
That feedback helped the council make a small improvement.

gaps.explanation: “The most common suggestion was a protected route” follows the council asking residents and is followed by what many people said.
“In response, they planned a route away from the main road” answers the residents’ worry about the busy shopping street.
“Local cyclists were invited to test the lane” follows the work and leads to what happened in the first week.
“That feedback helped the council make a small improvement” follows cyclists reporting problems and leads to the moved sign.
“The council is also offering free bicycle lessons” follows the parents using the route and leads to the next plan. Sentence D would only fit straight after the sign was moved.

parts.title: Getting around without a car
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word or phrase for each gap.
parts.passage: More people in our town are choosing to [1] the bus to work. A new travel app makes it easier to [2] when buses arrive. The council has also [3] a lower price for weekly tickets. Some people still find the bus [4] at busy times, so extra services will start next month. If the plan is successful, there may be [5] cars on the road and the air could be much [6].

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: We take the bus; do, make and go do not combine with “the bus” in this way.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: You check when buses arrive using an app.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: A council introduces a lower price; the other verbs do not fit.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: At busy times a bus is crowded, which means full of people.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: We use “fewer” with countable plural nouns such as cars.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: “Much cleaner” is the comparative form after “much”.

parts.title: A shared garden
parts.instructions: Complete the text with one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Our street has a small garden [1] to the library. It was empty [2] several years, so local people decided to use it. Everyone can help, even [3] they have only a little time. We usually meet [4] Saturday morning and share the jobs. Some neighbours grow flowers, [5] others look after the vegetables. We hope the garden will become a place [6] people can relax together.

gaps.explanation: Next to the library means beside it.
We say “empty for several years” to show how long.
“Even if they have only a little time” means although it is possible that they do.
We use “on” with days: on Saturday morning.
“While” contrasts what two groups of neighbours do.
“Where” refers to the place and begins the clause about relaxing there.

parts.title: A town clean-up day
parts.instructions: Listen and complete the notes. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time in each gap.

turns.speaker: gemma
turns.text: Hello, everyone. I am Gemma, and I am organising our town clean-up day. We will meet at the library at nine o’clock on Saturday. Please wear old clothes because we will paint the wooden benches as well as collect litter. The council will provide bags and brushes. We will work in the park until one o’clock, then have lunch together. Bring a bottle of water, but sandwiches will be provided by the café. If you need to borrow gloves, tell me when you arrive.

gaps.explanation: Gemma says they will meet at the library at nine on Saturday.
The clean-up day is on Saturday.
She asks everyone to wear old clothes because they will paint.
They will paint the wooden benches as well as collect litter.
Volunteers should bring a bottle of water.
The sandwiches will be provided by the café.

parts.title: An interview with a town planner
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Gareth, why did you become a town planner?

turns.speaker: gareth
turns.text: I studied geography at college. During a work placement, I helped improve a small square near a school. People used it more after we added seats and trees, and I wanted to do similar work.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What is your current project?

turns.speaker: gareth
turns.text: We are planning a safer route for people walking to the hospital. The main challenge is the busy morning traffic.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you know what local people need?

turns.speaker: gareth
turns.text: We organise meetings and ask residents to complete surveys. We also speak with shop owners because they understand how the area changes during the day.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What part of your work do you enjoy?

turns.speaker: gareth
turns.text: Seeing people use a place that we have improved. Even a small change can make a daily journey easier.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What advice would you give someone interested in this job?

turns.speaker: gareth
turns.text: Learn to listen carefully and explain your ideas clearly. Plans only work when people understand them.
